title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Fed hiked rates 25bp to 3.75%-4% Wednesday - first hike since 2023 - under new Chair Kevin Warsh; stocks sold off (Dow -1.2%, S&P -0.5%) but futures rebounded Thursday (S&P +0.6%) as Warsh's inflation resolve reassured bond markets.

Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield topped 5% (highest since 2007) and the 2-year hit its highest since 2024 after Warsh warned 'inflation is too high and has been for too long'; Brent crude fell ~3% to just under $106/bbl.
Companies: OpenAI is in early talks for a new funding round that could value it above $1.2 trillion (vs. $852B in March), ahead of an IPO now expected next year.
Companies: Novo Nordisk is partnering with Anthropic's Claude Science platform to speed AI-driven drug discovery for its Ozempic/Wegovy pipeline.

Companies: AI safety rift widens - Microsoft AI chief Suleyman blasted Anthropic's approach to training Claude around 'consciousness,' while Altman said the industry can handle AI risks and the Trump administration cast the 'effective altruism' AI-safety movement as an ideological threat.
Macro/Policy: The White House called the Fed's hike 'rather unfortunate,' underscoring the growing rift between Chair Warsh's inflation-fighting stance and the administration's push for lower rates.
